## Known Error Codes

A code's value is also its i18n message key, so each row carries the message the API actually answers with. `Message` is the base bundle (the fallback every locale resolves through); a `Message (<tag>)` column is that locale's own bundle. An em dash means that bundle has no entry for that code.

"Consumer note" is the error-code constant's own Javadoc, verbatim apart from markup — when the module's author documented what raises the code and what makes it stop being raised, that is what it says.

"Raised by" counts the endpoints whose controller → service → domain call walk reaches a throw site naming the code. An unbound code is thrown only from code no endpoint's walk reaches (a cross-module entry point, a job, or a call past the walk's depth) — it is listed, not attributed.

| Code | Value | Source | Message | Status | HTTP Status | Raised by | Consumer note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONNECTION_NOT_ACTIVATED | `REG-SERVE-CONNECTION-NOT-ACTIVATED` | contract/ServeRefusalCodes.java | — |  |  | no throw site naming it in module source | RULE-REG-017 — the current version of a service names a connection the environment does not register (ServiceConnectionNotActivatedException). |
| SERVICE_NOT_FOUND | `REG-404-SERVICE-NOT-FOUND` | error/ServiceRegistryErrorCodes.java | The service "{serviceCode}" is not available. |  | 404 NOT_FOUND | 1 endpoint(s) — see their Business Responses | RULE-REG-016 — the service code is not held by the registry (API-REG-002). |
| UNEXPECTED_FAILURE | `REG-500` | error/ServiceRegistryErrorCodes.java | The service registry could not complete the request. |  | 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR | 2 endpoint(s) — see their Business Responses | PLATFORM-STD — an unexpected server failure (API-REG-001 … API-REG-003). |
